visualReview.notes: Inspected all seven final portable views against individually viewed local 2014 and 2016 photographs, official city designation photographs and current NPS visitor-center photograph. Both 51 and 53 retain their contrasting stucco upper facades, three/four casement bays, brick storefronts and arched entrances. Review corrected the solid residential door at 53, light visitor-center entrance framing at 51 and foundations along the falling rear terrain.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected all seven final shared-material views and the full front view. Brick, stucco, stone, membrane and painted metal use metric shared bindings; glass and pride flags use separate local palettes. Door relief, window baskets and storefront lettering remain readable without copied photo pixels. Flat terrain here is a material fixture; independent terrain remains in the portable scene.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected all nineteen final lighting, quality and forced-detail views. Skyline preserves the paired building masses and stepped roofs; district adds storefront openings and upper windows; street and closeup retain baskets, door framing and original lettering. Synthetic neighbors are style fixtures. No physical-device frame-rate measurement is claimed.

geographicReview.notes: Both individual mapped footprints at 51–53 Christopher Street are retained; taller neighboring buildings are excluded. Anchor [-74.00212794542313,40.73391432195926], heading 0.191648856603142: +X east-northeast along Christopher Street and +Z south-southeast toward the street. Independent Terrarium terrain remains unchanged, datum 6.4416 m at sidewalk [-1.8,15.1]. Foundations reach -2.2 m to accommodate the rearward ground fall. Mapped heights of 6 and 7.4 m are coarse controls; photographs guide parapet heights. Footprint suppression remains off; another host DEM can differ.

fidelityReview.notes: Individually inspected local 2014/2016 photographs, official city designation photograph and boundary map, and a current NPS photograph. Current visitor-center framing replaces the former salon frontage. Vertical dimensions, hidden rear upper-story termination, roof equipment and skylight spacing remain approximations. Window baskets, pride flags, lanterns and lettering are original simplified geometry; no exact 1969 reconstruction, photo pixels or official visitor-center logo is claimed.

Simplified storefronts and upper windows reduce distant detail while preserving both building silhouettes. Error values are authoring budgets, not measured mesh deviations.

geometryValidation.notes: Exact regeneration, ordinary import verification, four current LOD checks and strict medium-fi audit passed. Source bundle, scene and terrain schemas pass; independent terrain PNG encoding error is recorded above. No independent Khronos-validator run is claimed.

limitations: Original medium-fi exterior of 51–53 Christopher Street, using individually inspected local 2014/2016 photos, official city designation photo/map and current NPS visitor-center photograph. No exact 1969 reconstruction.
Both individual mapped footprints are retained; taller neighboring buildings, interiors, crowds and temporary banners are excluded.
Vertical dimensions and hidden rear/roof details are approximations. The 51 rear-wing upper-story termination, skylight spacing and equipment positions are interpreted from limited evidence.

Small pride flags, window baskets, lanterns and storefront lettering are simplified original geometry. The red sign is colored geometry, not a physically simulated neon tube. No photo pixels or official visitor-center logos are embedded.
Map heights are coarse controls, with parapets interpreted from facade photographs. Independent terrain is unchanged; exact contact can differ with another host DEM.
